figures.name: Lincoln's second inauguration, 1865
figures.alt: Abraham Lincoln reads his second inaugural address from a platform on the east front of the Capitol, above a dense crowd, on 4 March 1865.

figures.at: Perhaps the people who built the first furnaces
figures.name: Coalbrookdale by Night, 1801
figures.credit: Philip James de Loutherbourg, Science Museum, London
figures.alt: Iron furnaces at Coalbrookdale light the night sky with fire and smoke while horses haul a cart along the road below.

figures.at: Perhaps the people who split the atom
figures.name: The Castle Bravo hydrogen bomb, 1954
figures.alt: The fireball of Castle Bravo, the largest American nuclear test, rising through a red sky above the clouds over Bikini Atoll in March 1954.

figures.at: I hope this demo has shown
figures.name: Pale Blue Dot, 1990
figures.alt: The Earth as a single pale dot inside a band of scattered sunlight, seen by Voyager 1 from about six billion kilometres away.

pics.name: The Battle of Lexington, 1775
pics.credit: William Barnes Wollen (1910), National Army Museum
pics.alt: Militiamen on Lexington Green fire through musket smoke at a line of British regulars, while others tend the wounded and the dead.

pics.name: The Peterloo Massacre, 1819
pics.alt: A print of the Peterloo Massacre: cavalry with raised sabres ride down a crowd of men, women and children in Manchester, 16 August 1819.

pics.name: Chartists on Kennington Common, 1848
pics.alt: One of the first photographs of a crowd: Chartists massed on Kennington Common in London to demand the vote, 10 April 1848.
